IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert (perf-canary): `runtime-scheduler-canary` queue depth sustained high

- Cluster: perf-canary-usw2
- Build: `runtime-1.19.0-canary.23`
- Signal: `scheduler.queue_depth{class=short}` p95 increased + `request.wait_time_ms` p95 increased
- Started: ~5 min ago
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/runtime-scheduler/mixed-workload?var=cluster=perf-canary-usw2&var=build=runtime-1.19.0-canary.23
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/SRE/Mixed+workload+scheduler+canary+runbook

Rafael Mendes: looking. is this only canary slice? any customer traffic on that pool?

Aisha Bello: it’s the perf-canary job slice only (internal). prod dedicated not impacted.

Rafael Mendes: ok. i’m seeing short queue depth pinned ~2.5k, long queue ~0, and GPU util oscillating. wait time p95 jumped from ~18ms to ~140ms right when canary.23 rolled.

Sean Gallagher: can we confirm whether the mixed-workload scheduler flag is on for this canary? last i saw it should be A/B.

Connor O'Brien: deploy note: canary.23 picked up new default config for the perf-canary job. it *may* have flipped the flag to on for 100% of canary instead of A/B (need to verify).

Sofia Ivanova: flag should be default-off, but perf-canary job template can override. what’s the config on the pod?

Omar El-Sayed: checking logs. seeing `scheduler_policy=mixed_workload_two_queue` in structured logs. also seeing a bunch of sampled decisions: `dequeue_class=long` taking >400ms occasionally.

Julian Moore: note the queue depth panel is per-class; short queue rising but long queue is not actually zero—looks like it’s blocked behind prefill batches, so it’s not being enqueued? could be admission path / backpressure.

Marcus Reed: i can repro locally with the same trace: when a long prefill batch starts, we hold the scheduler lock longer and short dequeues stall. queue depth goes up fast under burst.

Rafael Mendes: this looks like a priority inversion: short requests are waiting behind a long prefill dispatch. any changes in canary.23 around batching/dispatch?

Sofia Ivanova: canary.23 includes the “two-queue dispatch + starvation guardrails” patch set. we also changed the enqueue path to tag class earlier. if lock is held across prefill batch construction, that’s a bug.

Sean Gallagher: classification issue vs lock contention vs backpressure—either way, we should rollback canary build to stop noisy graphs. impact is internal but it’s tripping alerts.

Aisha Bello: +1. also queue depth alert threshold is paging in this channel, so let’s stabilize and then debug.

Rafael Mendes: proposing immediate action:
1) rollback perf-canary job to canary.22
2) set `runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled=false` explicitly in perf-canary config (until we re-enable A/B)
3) open follow-up PR for lock/priority inversion + add regression test

Connor O'Brien: i can trigger rollback now. confirm ok to revert deployment `runtime-scheduler-canary` to `runtime-1.19.0-canary.22`?

Sean Gallagher: approved. do it.

DeployBot: Deployment started: `runtime-scheduler-canary` -> image `runtime-1.19.0-canary.22`

Omar El-Sayed: while rollback runs, quick datapoint: the spike started exactly when `mixed_workload` went from 50% to 100% on that job. so config drift explains the severity.

Julian Moore: i’m also seeing `scheduler.wait_time_ms{class=short}` is bimodal. suggests we’re occasionally blocking short queue entirely. that’s consistent with the “short blocked behind long prefill batch” hypothesis.

Tomáš Novák: if we’re going to keep alerting on perf-canary, can we add a note in runbook: “if build flips policy to 100%, expect queue depth changes; validate A/B label first”?

Aisha Bello: yes. but ideally the canary job should always publish the A/B label in the metric so we can filter. right now it’s just build tag + cluster.

Sofia Ivanova: agree. for the code fix: the dispatch loop should not hold the global scheduler lock while building/merging the prefill microbatch. we can snapshot queue head under lock, release, build batch, then reacquire for dequeue commit. Marcus can you take that?

Marcus Reed: yup. i’ll open a PR today. will also add a regression test: “short requests never wait >X ms behind a long prefill under load” using the simulation harness.

Rafael Mendes: once rollback completes, please post graph screenshots in the incident ticket (or just link the dashboard time range). also we should record this as “minor incident-style investigation” for the project retro.

DeployBot: Deployment finished: `runtime-scheduler-canary` now running `runtime-1.19.0-canary.22`

Omar El-Sayed: graphs recovering. short queue depth dropping from 2.5k -> 200 over last 2 min. wait time p95 back to ~20ms.

Aisha Bello: alert is clearing. no further paging.

Sean Gallagher: great. next steps:
- Connor: audit the perf-canary job config and ensure scheduler flag is truly A/B next time; add guardrail so it can’t go 100% without explicit approval.
- Sofia/Marcus: follow-up PR for priority inversion / lock contention + regression test. tag SRE for review.
- Julian/Omar: add a metric for “scheduler lock hold time” or “dispatch critical section duration” if we can.

Connor O'Brien: ack. i’ll patch the perf-canary pipeline to enforce A/B split and expose `policy_variant` label. will file a small PR in perf-canary repo.

Julian Moore: for metrics naming, i’ll propose `runtime.scheduler.lock_hold_us` histogram + `runtime.scheduler.dispatch_batch_build_ms` for the slow path. will sync with Allison’s observability conventions later.

Rafael Mendes: can someone drop the commit/build diff between canary.22 and canary.23 here? just to attach to notes.

Sofia Ivanova: canary.23 = includes PRs: two-queue dispatch + starvation guardrails + per-class admission thresholds. the problematic part is likely in dispatch where we build prefill microbatch while holding `scheduler_mu`. Marcus will point to exact hunk in PR.

Marcus Reed: will do. PR incoming shortly; i’ll link here + in ENG-4823/ENG-4827.

Tomáš Novák: i’ll update runbook with “rollback steps” + “how to confirm whether the flag is on” (`scheduler_policy` log field + configmap key).

Sean Gallagher: closing this out as mitigated (internal canary only). please keep thread updated with PR link + when we plan to re-enable canary.23.

Aisha Bello: also adding a temporary alert mute for 30 min while things settle; not expecting more spikes now that we’re back on .22.
